sections.title: Chart the notices, mark the disables
sections.body:
> A reviewer should see the readings that matter at a glance, and see which one tripped the disable.

```
domain-enforcement → main, in merge order
1  feat(loo-6239): add hourly notice readings query
   2  feat(loo-6239): chart notices by type                 ↳ builds on 1
      3  feat(loo-6239): return the notice chart for review ↳ builds on 2
         4  feat(loo-6239): chart notices on domain review  ↳ builds on 3
            5  chore(loo-6239): stop loading notice rows    ↳ builds on 4
            6  feat(loo-6239): mark disables on the chart   ↳ builds on 4   (new, not gated yet)
```

Branches 1–5 are gates-green, waiting for you to push. Branch 6 hasn't been reviewed or gated.

Sign off on each branch page. A note there is review feedback on that branch.

sections.title: Add hourly notice readings query
sections.body:
> One row per hour and type: the highest rate that hour, the bad-email count of that same reading, and the worst level.

The cron writes a reading every 15 minutes. The query folds four readings into one point:

```
AccountLimitNotice (Spam, one hour)              listHourlyForTeam → one row
──────────────────────────────────────           ──────────────────────────────────
09:07  Warning   4 / 1000  = 0.40%               hour       09:00
09:22  Error     3 /  500  = 0.60%   ← peak      type       Spam
                                                 peakRate   0.006
                                                 peakNumerator  3   (from the 0.60% reading,
                                                                     not the larger 4)
                                                 worstLevel Error
                                                 readings   2
```

**Changes**
- New `listHourlyForTeam` in `queries/account-limit-notice.ts` (one raw SQL group-by).
- New test factory `createAccountLimitNotice`, and three query tests against the real DB.

**Holds because** the count is taken from the peak-rate reading (`array_agg … ORDER BY rate`), so the rate and count always come from the same reading. A reading with 0 deliveries has no rate (`nullif`) instead of dividing by zero.

**Watch for** levels order by enum position (Info < Warning < Error), so `max(level)` is the worst one.

sections.title: Chart notices by type
sections.body:
> Split the hours into one series per type, with the three things a reviewer reads first: the peak, the hours at Warning or Error, and the last Error.

```
chartForTeam({ teamId, since }) →
{
  since: 2026-10-29 00:00,  until: now,          ← one shared time axis
  series: [
    { type: "Spam",
      peakRate: 0.0042, warningHours: 1, errorHours: 2, lastErrorAt: 11:00,
      points: [ { hour: 09:00, rate: 0.002,  count: 2, level: "Warning" },
                { hour: 10:00, rate: 0.0042, count: 5, level: "Error" },
                { hour: 11:00, rate: null,   count: 1, level: "Error" } ] },  ← no deliveries
    { type: "Bounce", peakRate: 0.01, warningHours: 0, errorHours: 0, lastErrorAt: null, … }
  ]
}
```

**Changes**
- New `models/account-limit-notice.ts` with `chartForTeam`; `now` is injected.
- Three model tests with fake deps and no DB.

**Holds because** `peakRate` skips hours without a rate, and is `null` when no hour had one, never 0.

sections.title: Return the notice chart for review
sections.body:
> The domain review's query returns the chart for the same window as everything else on the page.

```
admin.getDomainInfo  →  {
  domain, recentSuspiciousActivity,
  recentAccountLimitNotices,                 (still here, removed in branch 5)
+ accountLimitNoticeChart: { since, until, series[] },
  disabledEmailMessages
}
```

**Changes**
- One call in `getDomainInfo`: `chartForTeam({ teamId: domain.teamId, since: cutoffDate })`.

**Holds because** `since` is the same cutoff the page's time filter already uses, so the chart and the other sections cover the same window.

sections.title: Chart notices on domain review
sections.body:
> Replace the wall of notice cards with one small chart per type, and make Error impossible to miss.

**Before**: one card per non-Info reading. While a team sits at Warning or Error, that's 4 cards an hour for each type.

```
┌ Spam · Error  0.41%  Oct 28 15:07 ┐
┌ Spam · Error  0.38%  Oct 28 14:52 ┐
┌ Bounce · Warning  1.62%  14:52    ┐
┌ Spam · Error  0.44%  Oct 28 14:37 ┐
  … one per 15 minutes, for the whole window
```

**After**: one chart per type that has readings in the window.

```
╔ Spam complaints  per non-Gmail delivery  [Error]  peak 0.42% · 5 h at Error · last Error 3 PM ╗
║                                   ●●●                                                         ║
║                                 ●     ●                                                       ║
║ ·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─╱───────╲─·─·─·─·─·─·─·                                        ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ ▸ Hourly readings ══╝
┌ Hard bounces  per delivery ───────────────────────── peak 2.20% · 3 h at Warning ┐
│          ○○○                                                                    │
│ ·─·─·─·─╱───╲─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ▸ Hourly readings ┘
  · Info hour   ● Error   ○ Warning   hover: "0.42% · 105 bad emails at peak · Error"
```

**Changes**
- New `components/admin/AccountLimitNoticeChart.tsx`: one SVG per type, the line broken at gaps, hover on the nearest hour, and the hourly table behind a `<details>`.
- `DomainReview.tsx`: the "Account Limit Notices" section renders the chart.

**Behavior change** the chart includes Info readings, which the card list filtered out, so you can see the baseline. "Peak" is per hour, not per 15-minute reading.

**Watch for** not yet looked at in a real browser before tonight's preview.

sections.title: Stop loading notice rows for review
sections.body:
> Once the chart exists, nothing on the review page reads the raw rows, so the query stops loading them.

```
admin.getDomainInfo  →  {
  domain, recentSuspiciousActivity,
- recentAccountLimitNotices,          ← every non-Info row in the window
  accountLimitNoticeChart,
  disabledEmailMessages
}
```

**Changes**
- Drops the `recentAccountLimitNotices` query and the now-unused `AccountLimitNoticeLevel` import.
- `AccountLimitNoticeItem` (the card) is still used by the team breakdown feed. Its prop type now comes from that feed's own query, `listTeamAccountLimitNotices`, instead of the deleted field.

**Holds because** typecheck: any remaining reader of the deleted field would fail to compile.

sections.title: Mark domain disables on the notice chart
sections.body:
> Draw each disable of this domain on the charts, so the reviewer sees which reading tripped it without matching timestamps.

```
╔ Spam complaints  per non-Gmail delivery  [Error] ═══════════════ peak 0.42% · 5 h at Error ╗
║        ┆                                  ┃●●                                             ║
║        ┆                                ● ┃  ●                                            ║
║ ·─·─·─·┆·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─·─╱──┃───╲─·─·─·─·─·                                 ║
╚════════┆══════════════════════════════════┃═════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
         ┆ earlier disable · Reenable        ┃ this disable (under review)
         dashed grey                         solid red
  hover that hour: "Domain disabled 3:42 PM (this review)"
```

**Changes**
- `AccountLimitNoticeChart` takes `disables` and `currentDisableId`, and draws a vertical line for each disable inside the window.
- `DomainReview` passes `domain.disableDomainEvents`, which `getDomainInfo` already returned, so the API doesn't change.

**Holds because** only disables inside `since…until` are drawn, so a line is always on the axis.

**Watch for** a disable shows on every type's chart, including types that had nothing to do with it. That's intentional: the line answers "when", and the red dots answer "which".
